dedupe_keys.name: combined effects of future urban growth and climate change on irrigation water demand in central arizona

description: Zhaocheng Wang and Enrique Vivoni at Arizona State University publish simulated irrigation demand for the Phoenix metropolitan area. VIC simulations originally used 1-kilometre cells and hourly timesteps over 1981–2100, but the deposited results are aggregated to 30-year averages. Baseline.zip uses 2010 land cover; ICLUS2050.zip and ICLUS2100.zip contain projected land-cover cases. NetCDF file names distinguish SSP2 or SSP5 development, RCP4.5 or RCP8.5 climate forcing, and eight climate models. The February 2022 deposit is free under CC BY 4.0. These averages can compare long-term irrigation-capacity needs under urban growth and climate scenarios. They cannot recover hourly demand peaks from the original simulations, and detailed averaging-window boundaries and units remain unknown from the summary. The describing paper was labelled in revision in the deposit. No related catalogue record explicitly identifies this Phoenix output collection, and files were not inspected.
